subject: Aster Health — multi-year prepay terms, ramp schedule & refund/co-term options
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@asterhealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Torres <btorres@asterhealth.com>, procurement@asterhealth.com
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interest in multi-year prepay — questions on refunds/early term

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency/cost profile looked promising. We are evaluating a multi-year prepay to lock unit economics for our clinical triage feature. A few items we need clarity on before procurement builds an internal business case: 

- If we do a 3-year annual prepay (paid at each year start), what is Redwood's stance on pro-rata refunds if we terminate early?
- Do you support co-terming across multiple contracts (we may consolidate other product spend later)?
- Can you share an example ramp schedule (token ramp) and how discounts change over time?

Appreciate a short note and any templates (term sheet / schedule) you can share.

Best,
Sophie
Procurement Lead, Aster Health

Attachment: (none)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@asterhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interest in multi-year prepay — questions on refunds/early term

Sophie — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Short answers up front, followed by an attached example schedule and the current MSA redline for reference.

1) Refunds / early termination: Our standard 3-year prepay is structured as annual prepayments with a two-way exit: if Aster terminates without cause in year 2 or 3, refunds are available on a pro-rata basis less a termination fee (typically 10% of remaining committed value) to cover rebalancing and reserved capacity. If Redwood initiates termination for convenience, we offer a pro-rata refund for unused prepay. Exact language is negotiable — legal can accept reasonable edits on caps.

2) Co-terming: We support co-terming; best practice is to include a schedule that maps contract lines to the co-term date and apply a credit or debit at the co-term. We can offer a simplified co-terming credit for the first 12 months to smooth economics.

3) Ramp schedule & discounts: See attached spreadsheet — we typically recommend a front-loaded ramp credit in year 1 (e.g., 25% credit against Year 1 consumption until you hit committed run-rate), then stepped unit discounts of 8%/6%/4% in years 1/2/3 on committed volume versus on-demand.

I've attached: Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.pdf and Prepay_Schedule_3yr_Aster.xlsx.

If ok, I'll loop in legal (Laura) to clarify the redline points that impact refunds/ET clauses and Marissa on pricing options for a 3-year vs annual prepay.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.pdf (PDF, excerpt), Prepay_Schedule_3yr_Aster.xlsx (XLSX, schedule sample)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@asterhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interest in multi-year prepay — questions on refunds/early term

Hi Sophie — looping in Laura (legal) and Dev (solutions) as discussed. A few operational notes: 

- From a commercial standpoint, we can consider reducing the termination fee to 5% if Aster commits to a minimum annual consumption floor and provides 45 days notice.
- For co-terming, we typically include a one-time reconciliation at co-term, with the ability to apply remaining prepay to consolidated contracts.
- Dev will propose a concrete ramp credit that keeps your effective first-year unit cost near the committed band while protecting Redwood's capacity planning.

Laura — Sophie asked specifically whether the refund language can be symmetrical (i.e., if Redwood changes service levels materially, Aster gets a symmetrical remedy). Sophie — does your procurement team have firm internal constraints (e.g., they require refunds to be 'without penalty')? That will drive the legal approach.

Cheers,
Marissa
Head of Sales, Enterprise

Attachment: (none)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@asterhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-13T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interest in multi-year prepay — questions on refunds/early term

Sophie — I put together a simple ramp schedule (attached) and a worked example of monthly token draw vs committed baseline. Key callouts: 

- Recommend a 3-step ramp credit: 25% credit until run-rate reached; 12% uplift months 4-12; standard committed discount thereafter. This preserves forecast accuracy for us while giving you breathing room.
- If co-terming happens and you move additional spend in year 2, we can apply a pro-rata top-up credit so Year 3 economics aren't penalized.
- On refunds: the mechanics we often use are an "available credit" pool that converts to a cash refund only after 12 months, which reduces churn risk and avoids frequent cash adjustments.

Attached: Prepay_Schedule_3yr_Aster.xlsx (updated with worked example). Happy to run this against Aster's expected monthly consumption if you share a simple forecast.

Thanks,
Dev
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Prepay_Schedule_3yr_Aster.xlsx (updated)

From: Aster Procurement <procurement@asterhealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@asterhealth.com>, Ben Torres <btorres@asterhealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-15T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aster Health — multi-year prepay terms, ramp schedule & refund/co-term options

Rishi / team — thanks for the materials. Procurement and finance reviewed the attached MSA redline and have two sticking points that require legal alignment before we can move to a term sheet: 

1) Early termination: Our standard policy is full pro-rata refund of unused prepay without a separate termination fee. We understand operational costs, but could you accept a 2% administrative fee instead of the 10% proposed?

2) Renewal / co-terming: We need a guaranteed mechanism to carry forward unused prepay across co-terming events without losing the original discount band. We can accept a reconciliation audit clause but not a unilateral re-pricing at co-term.

Ben (CFO) is copied — he is ok with a 3-year duration if economics are fixed for the term and there is a predictable refund path.

Please advise next steps and, if possible, send an MSA redline that reflects a 2% admin fee and the carry-forward mechanics so our legal team can perform a final pass.

Regards,
Aster Procurement Team

Attachment: Aster_MSA_comments_20260515.pdf (procurement redlines)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Aster Procurement <procurement@asterhealth.com>, Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@asterhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aster Health — multi-year prepay terms, ramp schedule & refund/co-term options

Team — appreciate the prompt review and constructive asks. Quick summary of where we can move and the proposed next steps so procurement has one trackable option: 

- Early termination: Redwood is prepared to reduce the administrative fee to 3% of remaining unearned prepay (instead of 10%) if Aster agrees to a minimum annual consumption floor (we propose 60% of Year 1 committed volume). If Aster prefers no floor, we can keep the 5% alternative. Laura — will prepare the exact language.

- Co-terming / carry-forward: We can accept a carry-forward mechanism that preserves the original discount band for any remaining prepay at co-term, subject to a one-time reconciliation audit within 90 days. Redwood will not unilaterally re-price carried-forward amounts.

- Ramp credits: Dev's front-loaded schedule remains — we'll apply a one-time Year 1 ramp credit equal to 20% of Year 1 prepay drawn against initial consumption; the spreadsheet attached shows the P&L impact.

Next steps: Laura will issue a revised MSA redline reflecting the 3% admin fee option and the carry-forward clause; Marissa and I will prepare a term sheet showing the 3-year schedule, with an alternative 12-month prepay option for CFO review. Sophie — if those moves are acceptable, could you confirm by EOD Monday so we can route to Laura for redline?

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_v4.pdf (to be issued by legal), Prepay_Schedule_3yr_Aster.xlsx (final proposal)
